title: A Ember for the Thorn
premise: Emrys Iversen fled his hedge-witch mistress to hide in Thornvale, a valley where magic cannot cross its borders, believing invisibility was safety. When a mute child arrives speaking the Old Tongue—the language that binds crowns—Emrys learns the child is a living seal, and the thing wearing King Aldric's crown is unraveling it to free itself. Guided by the witch he abandoned, Emrys must choose between loyalty to the valley that sheltered him and the truth that his own bloodline created the binding. In the end, Emrys unbinds the king not by destroying the creature but by taking its place as the new seal, trading his freedom for Aldric's, while the child carries word of his sacrifice back into the valley.
about_author: Edmund Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in obligations older than themselves.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Two years after fleeing his apprenticeship, Emrys lives quietly in Thornvale, mending fences and refusing to remember the magic he left behind. A storm brings a barefoot child to his door, speaking words that ache in his bones—a language he knows only from his mistress's forbidden books. The beat: comfort shattered, the past knocking literally at his threshold.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with an interlude from the child, Wren. Fleeing the valley with Wren, Emrys reaches the capital and witnesses King Aldric—hollow-eyed, speaking in two voices—as the entity beneath the crown drains Wren's seal. His old mistress Maeve finds them, offering help laced with bitter reproach. The beat: guilt sharpened into resolve; Emrys accepts duty he never wanted.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Maeve's POV during the ritual in the throne room. As she and Emrys work the counter-binding, the entity reveals the truth: the original seal was forged by an Iversen, and only Iversen blood can renew it. Aldric briefly surfaces, begging for death over servitude. The entity offers Emrys escape—walk away, let the kingdom burn. The beat: climax of choice, love against duty as Emrys refuses both cowardice and easy mercy.

chapters.title: An Ember Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The binding remade, Emrys stands as the new seal within the throne room's heart, alive but bound, visited by Maeve and by Wren, who has found a home in the palace. Aldric, freed, kneels to his rescuer. Wren begins teaching the court the Old Tongue so no seal will ever be made in ignorance again. The beat: bittersweet resolution—sacrifice transmuted into legacy, and love persisting beyond walls.
